parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states that no function from ℂ (the Euclidean plane ℝ²) to Fin 5 gives distinct colors to every pair of points at Euclidean distance exactly 1. No measurability or other regularity is imposed on the color classes. This matches the main claim of Theorem 1.1, χ(ℝ²) ≥ 6 for arbitrary colorings. The main caveat concerns coverage only: the upper bound χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7 and the intermediate theorems (transfer, weak measurable coloring) are not formalized.

glossary.plain: A map c : ℂ → {0,…,k−1} such that for all x, y ∈ ℂ with |x − y| = 1 we have c(x) ≠ c(y).
glossary.standard_concept: Proper k-coloring of the unit-distance graph of the Euclidean plane
glossary.note: The norm on ℂ is the complex modulus, which equals the Euclidean norm on ℝ². Subtraction is in ℂ, so nothing truncates.

lean_claims.plain: There is no function c : ℂ → Fin 5 such that c(x) ≠ c(y) for all x, y ∈ ℂ with |x − y| = 1.

paper_claims.plain: The Euclidean plane has no proper five-coloring, even with arbitrary color classes. Consequently 6 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7.
For every positive integer k, a proper k-coloring of ℝ² exists iff a weak measurable k-coloring exists.
There is no weak measurable five-coloring of the plane.

coverage.why: The non-existence of a proper 5-coloring (hence χ ≥ 6) is formalized exactly. The upper bound χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7 is not stated.

flags.explanation: Only the lower-bound half of Theorem 1.1 is formalized. The upper bound χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7 (Isbell/Hadwiger hexagonal coloring) is classical and is not part of the Lean statement.

lint_verdicts.why: The subtraction `point - otherPoint` is in ℂ, not ℕ, so no truncation occurs.
